response: A young snapshot starting between early enrollment and demotion cannot miss live young targets because `cell.rs:588-605` restricts early enrollment to a prepared guard where `Trace::edges_rooted_before_unroot` certifies `Owner::Root` (`gc.rs:1053`, now checked across every `Vec` element at `collector/trace_impls.rs:76`) and subsequent ordinary root demotion invokes deletion barriers, leaving only the bounded caveats that all other `Trace` implementations must faithfully certify every edge and the prepared guard must already expose those edges before a snapshot can drain and clear the dirty owner prior to demotion. For a stale primary prune racing across overflow insertion (`collector.rs:1953-1993`), non-rollback in `DirtyOwners::publish` and exact-`id` terminal-unlink removal protect unsaturated versions, but at a saturated mutation version the increment ceases to advance so a stale prune comparing versions—whether filtering overflow reconciliation with `<=` or pruning primary after overflow drains on version equality—cannot distinguish the newer enrollment from the stale state and can drop a dirty owner (an unsafe interleaving bounded only by version-saturation reachability unless pruning is suppressed at saturation).
